title: Regex-as-Grammar Parser (REGEX_AS_GRAMMAR_PARSER)
pattern: Using highly complex, nested, or unreadable regular expressions with capture groups as a substitute for a structured parser or recursive-descent grammar when reading nested, optional, or hierarchical formats.
why_bad: Regular expressions are non-composable; they cannot be cleanly combined to build larger formats. They are extremely hard to test and maintain, and small changes in target formats lead to silent capture-index mismatches. Moreover, they suffer from catastrophic backtracking bugs and fail on subtle quoting/escaping rules.
detection: Look for complex nested regular expressions (especially those containing multiple optional groups, lookaheads, or non-capturing groups) whose captured indices are manually parsed and converted to structure fields.
fix: Refactor to use a recursive-descent parser, parser combinators (e.g., `nom`), or a dedicated serialization library where format specifications are cleanly decoupled and composable.
source: *Chris Hanson & Gerald Sussman - Software Design for Flexibility (2021)*, Section 2.2; *Andrew Hunt & David Thomas - The Pragmatic Programmer, 20th Anniversary Edition (2019)*, Appendix 2 (Answer 8).
